identity.title: Near-infrared Imaging of a Spiral in the CQ Tau Disk

paper_type_evidence.quote: We also used an ALMA archival image, observed in Cycle 5 (ID: 2017.1.01404.S, PI: L. Testi), which achieved a noise level of $\sim$23 $\mu$Jy/beam

evidence.quote: CQ Tau (RA = 05:35:58.47, Dec = +24:44:54.1) is a YSO in the Taurus star forming region

question.value: Does the CQ Tau disk host a spiral or companion candidates in L'-band and H-band imaging, and what are its nature (thermal vs scattered) and origin?

evidence.quote: To further search for protoplanets as well as asymmetric features in the CQ Tau disk, we used two high-contrast imaging observations with Keck/NIRC2 and Subaru/AO188+HiCIAO.
observed in Cycle 5 (ID: 2017.1.01404.S, PI: L. Testi)
a beam size of 69 mas and 51 mas for major-axis and minor-axis, respectively
which achieved a noise level of $\sim$23 $\mu$Jy/beam
We also used an ALMA archival image, observed in Cycle 5 (ID: 2017.1.01404.S, PI: L. Testi)

provided.value: L'-band vortex coronagraph ADI imaging, 2018 Dec 24, 1800 s

evidence.quote: CQ Tau was observed on UT 2018 Dec 24 (PI: D. Mawet) using the Keck/NIRC2 vortex coronagraph
Subaru/AO188+HiCIAO observed CQ Tau in a combination of PDI and ADI as part of the SEEDS project

what.value: Disk inclination 35 deg and major-axis PA 55 deg

evidence.loc: Comparison of the Two Data Sets
evidence.quote: derived by (cite: Ubeira2019): $i=35\ensuremath{^\circ}$ and PA$_a = 55\ensuremath{^\circ}$

what.value: L'-band photometry used to convert ADU to surface brightness

evidence.quote: We converted ADU into the surface brightness using a previous $L^\prime$-band photometry (cite: McDonald2017)
$T_\star$=6900 K and $L_\star=10L_{\odot}$ (cite: Testi2001; Ubeira2019)
With the small grain surface density of 0.0375 g/cm$^2$ of CQ Tau’s disk (cite: Ubeira2019)

what.value: Details of the ALMA data set described elsewhere

evidence.quote: Details of this data set as well as other ALMA data of CQ Tau are described in (cite: Ubeira2019).

what.value: HiCIAO PDI reduction with IRAF pipeline as in earlier studies

evidence.quote: we reduced the polarimetric data sets by means of an `IRAF` pipeline, which was used in previous HiCIAO PDI studies (cite: Hashimoto2011; Hashimoto2012)

unstated_but_needed: ALMA calibration and imaging details (robust, CASA version) not given
VIP parameters beyond PC=8 and IWA=16 pix (FoV, PCA options)
Details of forward-model injection positions and fluxes

method.value: PCA-based ADI with VIP, PC=8, IWA=16 pix

evidence.quote: We adopted IWA=16 pix so that the asymmetric feature is reproduced with a higher SNR.

validation.value: Feature survives wide range of PC values

evidence.quote: The feature appears robust because it survives for a wide range of PC values

analysis_steps.goal: Fit spiral pitch angle in HiCIAO PI

method.value: Best-fit logarithmic spiral to radial maxima in 1 deg azimuthal bins of deprojected image

evidence.loc: Comparison of the Two Data Sets
evidence.quote: The trace was identified as radial maxima in azimuthal bins of $1\ensuremath{^\circ}$ in the image obtained after deprojection

method.value: Inject fake PSFs along fitted spiral and measure input/output flux ratio

evidence.loc: Comparison of the Two Data Sets
evidence.quote: We used the off-axis PSF of CQ Tau and injected fake PSFs at several separations and position angles to produce fake spiral features

method.value: Optically thick thermal balance for grain temperature; analytic scattered-light formula with single scattering

evidence.quote: Here, we assume $H(1,\omega_\nu)=1$ (single scattering) for simplicity.

assumptions.value: Gas-to-dust ratio 100; disk optically thick at L'

evidence.quote: We assume that the disk is optically thick at L$^\prime$-band.

used_for.value: PCA ADI reduction of NIRC2 data

evidence.quote: the data set was processed via the vortex image processing (cite: Gonzalez2017) package that applies principal component analysis (PCA) for the ADI reduction
we reduced the polarimetric data sets by means of an `IRAF` pipeline

evidence.loc: Comparison of the Two Data Sets
evidence.quote: The fitted result for the spiral (the central image in Figure [\[fig: HiCIAO\]](#fig: HiCIAO)) is $34\ensuremath{^\circ}\pm2\ensuremath{^\circ}$.

evidence.loc: Comparison of the Two Data Sets
evidence.quote: a flux recovered by a throughput of 0.54 at 50 au, which corresponds to 126 mJy/arcsec$^2$ at the brightest region in the spiral
the temperature of the grains is expected to be $T_{\rm grain}\sim$202.5K
the brightest region in this feature has 68$\pm$8.5 mJy/arcsec$^2$

findings_qualitative.value: No companion candidates detected; new spiral overlapping ALMA dust ring

evidence.quote: Apart from the spiral feature our observations could not detect any companion candidates.

claims.hypothesis: Is the L'-band spiral explained by scattering alone?
claims.experiment: Analytic scattered-light estimate vs observed brightness
claims.result: Predicted 8.5 mJy/arcsec2 vs much brighter observed
claims.finding: Thermal emission (~200 K) needed unless inner disk acts as light source

evidence.quote: The NIRC2 result, however, is much brighter than the expected brightness in $L^\prime$-band.

limitations_admitted.value: Pitch angle approximate due to inclination/projection effects

evidence.loc: Comparison of the Two Data Sets
evidence.quote: Therefore, our measurements of the arm pitch angles are approximations only.

referee_caveats_inferred: Single-scattering and optically thick assumptions crude

data_public_as_stated.value: ALMA archival data used; Subaru data via SMOKA

evidence.quote: obtained from the SMOKA, which is operated by the Astronomy Data Center

reproducibility.score_reason: ALMA only for overlay; IR data and recipe partly specified.
reproducibility.rediscovery_reason: ALMA minor and main results rely on non-ALMA IR data.
